assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Dentition
items.clue: The number, type, size and arrangement of an animal's teeth.

items.label: Archaea
items.clue: One of the three domains of life, alongside Bacteria and Eukaryota.

items.label: Epiphyte
items.clue: A plant that grows on the branches of a tree, high in the forest where light is available, without roots in the soil.

items.label: Heterotroph
items.clue: An organism that obtains carbon compounds from other organisms, living or dead, rather than synthesizing them from inorganic substances.

questions.stem: What is meant by the ecological niche of a species?

options.text: The role of the species in its ecosystem, including its biotic and abiotic interactions
The place where the species lives, described by its location and ecosystem type
The position of the species in a food chain, defined by the food it eats
The interactions of the species with other organisms, leaving out abiotic factors

questions.explanation: This is the guide's definition. A niche is a role, described by the biotic and abiotic interactions that influence the species' growth, survival and reproduction, including how it obtains food.

questions.stem: Which statement describes an obligate anaerobe?

options.text: An organism that does not use oxygen but is unharmed when oxygen gas is present
An organism that normally respires anaerobically but can use oxygen if needed
An organism that can grow only where oxygen gas is absent from its environment
An organism that switches to anaerobic respiration when its oxygen supply runs out

questions.explanation: Obligate anaerobes cannot tolerate oxygen gas. They are found only in oxygen-free environments, such as deep sediments or the gut, because oxygen prevents their growth.

questions.stem: In which groups of organisms is photosynthesis the mode of nutrition?

options.text: Plants, algae and several groups of photosynthetic prokaryotes such as cyanobacteria
Plants and algae only, because prokaryotes are unable to photosynthesize
Plants, algae and any prokaryotes whose cells happen to contain chloroplasts
Plants, algae and photosynthetic prokaryotes, though plants also feed from the soil

questions.explanation: Photosynthesis is the mode of nutrition of plants, of algae and of several groups of photosynthetic prokaryotes. All synthesize their own carbon compounds from carbon dioxide using light energy.

questions.stem: Which statement about nutrition in animals is correct?

options.text: Animals that host photosynthetic algae inside their cells are autotrophic
Animals assimilate their food by absorbing it across the lining of the gut
Animals are heterotrophs that ingest, digest, absorb and assimilate food
Animals ingest food when digested molecules pass into their cells

questions.explanation: All animals are heterotrophic. Their holozoic nutrition consists of ingestion of food, internal digestion, absorption of the products and their assimilation into the animal's tissues.

options.text: Secretion of enzymes onto dead organic matter, followed by absorption of the products of digestion
Ingestion of dead organic matter, followed by internal digestion and absorption of products
Any feeding on dead organic matter, whether by fungi and bacteria or by earthworms and woodlice
Synthesis of carbon compounds by fungi and bacteria that grow on dead organic matter

questions.stem: How were biologists able to deduce the diets of extinct hominids such as Paranthropus robustus?

options.text: By developing theories relating dentition to diet from the fossils themselves, then confirming them with living mammals
By comparing the size of the fossil jaws with those of living carnivores, since powerful jaws indicate meat-eating
By treating the question as unanswerable, since the diet of an extinct animal is a guess that cannot be tested
By applying theories relating dentition to diet, developed from observing living mammals, to the fossil teeth

questions.stem: Which pairing of a rainforest plant with its strategy for harvesting light is correct?

options.text: Liana: germinates on a high branch and grows roots down the trunk until they reach the soil
Epiphyte: absorbs water and carbon compounds from the xylem and phloem of the tree it grows on
Forest-floor herb: absorbs carbon compounds from decaying leaves instead of photosynthesizing
Strangler epiphyte: germinates high on a branch and later sends roots down to the soil

questions.stem: Shrubs and herbs grow on the floor of a forest beneath a closed canopy. How do these plants obtain enough light to survive?

options.text: They are shade tolerant, able to photosynthesize at the low light intensities reaching the floor
They obtain carbon compounds from the decaying leaf litter, so they need little light
They receive sugar from the canopy trees through underground fungal networks
They cannot; plants that fail to reach the canopy survive only until they are shaded
